raw_case_text:
A 52-year-old male of Asian-origin was referred for the diagnosis of multiple lesions in the oral cavity. The patient reported to be HIV-seropositive for 12 years, during which he did not follow the antiretroviral treatment adequately as he took medications on an intermittent basis. When the oral lesions first appeared, T CD4+ was 70 cells/mm3, and the patient changed his behaviour and adhered to the proposed treatment (Lamivudine, Tenofovir and Atazanavir). Four months after cART was initiated, the patient had significant improvement in the immune system and an increase in T CD4+ to 486 cells/mm3 together with undetectable viral load. Concomitantly, the patient observed an marked increase in the amount and size of the oral lesions, which began to be aesthetically and functionally inconvenient, even for daily routine activities, such as mastication. After four years living with the increase in the amount of oral mucosa lesions, the patient sought treatment.
The intraoral clinical examination detected extensive nodular lesions on the entire oral mucosa (i.e. palate, tongue, mouth floor, and alveolar, jugal and labial mucosa), extending to the oropharyngeal region. The lesions were asymptomatic, whitish and erythematous. The majority of the lesions, like those seen in the palate and tongue, were sessile and had a smooth surface, whereas the others were pedunculated and had papillary projections (Figures 1, 2 and 3).
Incisional biopsy was performed and the material obtained was sent for histopathological examination. The sections were stained with hematoxylin and eosin, revealing a mucosal fragment covered with parakeratinised stratified squamous epithelium and acanthosis areas forming either blunt or sharp projections, giving a papillomatous aspect to the epithelium. At higher magnification, one could observe the formation of micro-abscesses, clusters of neutrophils and diffuse presence of koilocyte-like cells (Figure 4). In addition, a tissue sample was submitted to DNA extraction and analyzed by INNO-Lipa HPV genotyping extra II test (INNO-Lipa Innogenetics N.V., Ghent, Belgium), as well as PCR sequencing with generic primers, revealing the presence of HPV-32.
Based on the clinical aspect of the lesions, histopathological findings and detection of HPV-32, it was possible to diagnose the presence of epithelial proliferation due to HPV infection. The unusual clinical presentation raised discussion on the lesions, suggesting that it might be a case of either focal epithelial hyperplasia (FEH), a lesion strongly associated with HPV-32,or condyloma acuminata aggravated by the syndrome of immune reconstitution (SIR).
Due to the extension of lesions in the patient and, consequently, the great number of surgical procedures that would be necessary, as well as the high viral infectivity rate (leading to the possibility of re-contamination of the mucosa during manipulation), treatment based on surgical removal was discarded. The treatment was initiated with topical application of podophyllin and trichloroacetic acid. Nevertheless, the long-term treatment unfortunately made adhesion difficult for the patient, who did not attend the appointments after some sessions.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 52-year-old Asian male with a 12-year history of HIV infection was referred for extensive, functionally and aesthetically debilitating warty and nodular lesions covering his entire oral cavity that had dramatically proliferated 4 months after starting combination antiretroviral therapy 4 years earlier.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV 12 years prior with years of intermittent ART adherence, the patient first noticed oral mucosal lesions when his CD4+ count fell to 70 cells/mm3, prompting strict adherence to lamivudine, tenofovir, and atazanavir. Within 4 months of regular cART—as his CD4+ count surged to 486 cells/mm3 and his HIV viral load became undetectable—the oral lesions underwent explosive proliferation in number and size across the entire oral cavity, interfering with mastication and aesthetics for 4 years before referral.
subjective.past_medical_history: 12-year history of HIV infection; previously poorly adherent to ART, followed for the past 4 years by strict adherence to lamivudine, tenofovir, and atazanavir.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for extensive painless intraoral nodules impairing mastication. Home medications: lamivudine, tenofovir, and atazanavir.

objective.physical_examination: Intraoral examination revealed innumerable asymptomatic whitish-to-erythematous nodular and papillomatous lesions carpeting the entire oral mucosa—including the hard and soft palate, tongue, floor of the mouth, alveolar ridges, buccal mucosa, and labial mucosa—and extending into the oropharynx. Palatal and lingual lesions were predominantly sessile and smooth-surfaced, whereas labial and buccal lesions were pedunculated with papillary projections.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count had increased from 70 cells/mm3 prior to regular cART to 486 cells/mm3 within 4 months of cART. Incisional oral mucosal biopsy histopathology demonstrated parakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium with marked papillomatous acanthosis forming blunt and sharp projections, epithelial microabscesses with neutrophilic clusters, and diffuse koilocytic changes. Tissue DNA extraction with INNO-LiPA HPV Genotyping Extra II and generic-primer PCR sequencing identified human papillomavirus genotype 32 (HPV-32).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Florid oral HPV-32-associated focal epithelial hyperplasia (Heck disease) / oral condylomata acuminata exacerbated by immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) following rapid CD4+ T-cell recovery (from 70 to 486 cells/mm3 with undetectable HIV viral load on lamivudine, tenofovir, and atazanavir) in a 52-year-old HIV-positive male. Due to pan-mucosal involvement and high risk of intraoperative viral autoinoculation precluding surgical excision, conservative chemical cauterization with serial topical applications of podophyllin and trichloroacetic acid was initiated; however, the patient defaulted from long-term follow-up after several sessions.
